topic: Electromagnetic Radiation and Planck's Quantum Theory
title: Light in Packets? Planck Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A phone gets a message through a wall, a microwave oven warms food, and a heater coil glows red. One kind of wave does all three. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we measure that wave and find the energy hidden in one packet of light.

You will see Maxwell's electromagnetic wave (1870): electric and magnetic fields at right angles, needing no medium and moving at c = 3.0 × 10^8 m s^-1. On the molecule bench a slowed-down wave shows wavelength and frequency (in hertz, after Heinrich Hertz) trading off while the speed stays fixed. We line up the electromagnetic spectrum from radio waves to gamma rays, with visible light from violet (400 nm, 7.50 × 10^14 Hz) to red (750 nm, 4.00 × 10^14 Hz), and build c = νλ and wavenumber step by step. A heated iron rod goes dull red, red, white and blue, and Planck (1900) explains it: energy comes in packets, E = hν, with h = 6.626 × 10^-34 J s. A worked example finds the energy of one 500 nm photon (3.98 × 10^-19 J), then the exam trap about nanometres, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 17 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
